draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Kabini! The backwaters of the Kabini reservoir are very rich in wildlife, especially in summer when the water drops and leaves grassy meadows behind.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have named food spots out here, so stock up before you leave Mysuru.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Kabini Forest Reserve forms the south-eastern part of Nagarahole National Park, known for herds of elephants and tigers.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit by the big Kabini reservoir and watch the backwaters, the grassy banks pull in wildlife.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Kabini starts in Wayanad, Kerala, where the Panamaram and Mananthavady rivers meet, before flowing east into Karnataka.

spots.name: Kabini River
spots.detail: Right here · Backwaters that turn into grassy meadows in summer

tips.title: Come in summer for wildlife.
tips.body: That's when the water recedes and the meadows along the backwaters fill with animals.

tips.title: Plan the drive.
tips.body: Kabini is 61 km from Mysuru and 205 km from Bengaluru.

story.title: A river from Wayanad
story.body: The Kabini rises in Wayanad, Kerala, flows east into Mysore district and joins the Kaveri.

story.title: The Kabini Dam
story.body: Near Sargur the river forms the huge Kabini Reservoir behind a dam 2,284 ft long, between the villages of Bichanahalli and Bidarahalli.

story.title: Wildlife favourite
story.body: The Kabini Forest Reserve is one of Karnataka's most popular wildlife spots, loved for its green landscape, big lake, elephants and tigers.
